title: RFC: Support registry withholding
body:
*[View all comments](https://triagebot.infra.rust-lang.org/gh-comments/rust-lang/rfcs/pull/4016)*

<!-- Thank you for trying to improve Rust through the RFC process! -->
<!-- Please add a short summary of your RFC below -->

This RFC adds a new, optional registry index field, `availability` (`available | quarantined | withdrawn`).
It also specifies how Cargo avoids resolving `withheld` versions and instead display status-aware errors.

This will allow registries like crates.io to use "quarantine" during security investigations to loudly freezes crate bytes, preventing installs, in a fully reversible way (unlike today's crate deletion). It also allows leaving behind permanent
tombstones for malicious crate removals.

title: RFC: document a strict `Future` contract that forbids snoozing
body:
Require a future's owner to poll it when it requests a wakeup, to avoid [snoozing] bugs like ["Futurelock"]. This RFC is a docs-only change, but this will have far-reaching consequences for a lot of common async patterns.

RFC #4020 is being submitted at the same time. It adds `poll_progress` to `AsyncIterator`, in part to satisfy the strict `Future` contract introduced in this RFC.

[snoozing]: https://jacko.io/snooze.html
["Futurelock"]: https://rfd.shared.oxide.computer/rfd/0609

title: RFC: add `poll_progress` to `AsyncIterator`
body:
Fix ["Barbara battles buffered streams"] and iterator variants of ["Futurelock"] by adding `poll_progress` to `AsyncIterator`. Define a strict `AsyncIterator` contract for when `poll_next` and `poll_progress` should be called, mirroring the strict `Future` contract in RFC #4019.

To avoid burying the lede: Effectively deprecating [`StreamExt::next`] will probably be the most controversial part of this RFC. See "What about `.next()`?" in the Drawbacks section.

["Barbara battles buffered streams"]: https://rust-lang.github.io/wg-async/vision/submitted_stories/status_quo/barbara_battles_buffered_streams.html
["Futurelock"]: https://rfd.shared.oxide.computer/rfd/0609
[`StreamExt::next`]: https://docs.rs/futures/latest/futures/stream/trait.StreamExt.html#method.next

title: Deprecate `std::env::{vars, args}`
body:
*[View all comments](https://triagebot.infra.rust-lang.org/gh-comments/rust-lang/rfcs/pull/4021)*

`std::env::args` and especially `std::env::vars` are footguns whose existence in the standard library contradicts modern best practices of standard library API design. They do the language user a disservice by obfuscating the handling of errors and elevating an ignorant and buggy approach above one that is correct and only marginally more verbose. Accordingly, deprecate `args` in favor of `args_os` and `vars` in favor of `vars_os`.

> [!IMPORTANT]
> Since RFCs involve many conversations at once that can be difficult to follow, please use review comment threads on the text changes instead of direct comments on the RFC.
